title: Prod Echopoint frontend ran ahead of its API: a per-push diff stranded #1006's backend
summary: echopoint #1006 (MCP permissions allow/deny, ADR-0042) merged at 16:06Z. Its main CI run went red on two frontend flakes, so its backend never built or deployed. The next four pushes were frontend-only. `detect_changes` diffed each push only against the previous push, so each reported `backend_changed=false`. The frontend-only deploy path then shipped #1006's web app to dev and prod, against an API that stayed on 8334a800 with ask mode and program runs. Echopoint has about zero users, so no customer impact is known. The fix diffs a push against the last commit a green run verified, so a red run's changes ride the next green push.

impact.text: From 16:24Z, the prod web app showed #1006's Allow/Deny MCP page and no program-run pages, while the prod API still served ask mode, `/program-runs/*` and `/allowed-tools/*`. The same skew existed on dev. A fourth frontend-only push (#1012) shipped at 18:34Z. No customer report and no known customer impact (Echopoint has about zero users). The #1006 migrations 117 and 118 waited with the backend.

numbers.label: frontend-only deploys to prod against the old API
time this mechanism stranded a backend (first: #860, 2026-11-13)

trigger: The frontend of 2207351b (#1010) reached prod at 16:24:11Z through Deploy Router run 45652997315, while the prod API stayed on 8334a800.
detection: The `echopoint-investigation` routine found the skew on its run, about two hours later, by comparing `/health` with `main`. No alert fires on a red main run or on an API commit that stays behind `main`. That alert is an open action of the 2026-11-23 SEV4 (A3, owned by a human, due 2026-12-07).
resolution: The routine first made the gate flow `Admin impersonation refusals` (fc768d01) accept both the old and the #1006 behaviour, so the #1006 deploy cannot turn the echopoint gate red. ci-workflows #62 added `last-success-sha.yml` and a `base_sha` input to `detect-changes.yml`. echopoint #1013 opted in. Its merge push changed `go.yml`, a backend pattern, so it built and deployed the stranded #1006 backend. Dev served it at 18:36Z, the echopoint gate passed at 18:40Z, and prod API and frontend were both on 7a390ffc at 18:41:58Z.

whys.problem: The prod web app shipped #1006's MCP Allow/Deny page while the prod API kept ask mode and program runs

because.text: Four frontend-only deploys shipped HEAD's frontend; #1006's backend image was never built
because.evidence: Deploy Router runs [45652997315](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/infra/actions/runs/45652997315), [45653697683](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/infra/actions/runs/45653697683), [45657051443](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/infra/actions/runs/45657051443) ran only `deploy-echopoint-frontend` and `-prod`; `/health` stayed 8334a800

because.text: `detect_changes` reported `backend_changed=false` for 2207351b, b5c6a51e, bc85aa39 and f09065ac
It diffed each push only against `github.event.before`, the previous push
A red run deploys nothing, and nothing carried its changes into the next push's diff
Change detection measured a push against the previous push, not against the last commit a green run verified and deployed
The frontend-only path promoted to prod without checking which API commit prod runs
because.evidence: echopoint `go.yml` `dispatch-frontend-deploy-dev` sends `promote_to_prod: true`; the Deploy Router frontend runs have no gate or API check

because.text: The frontend-only deploy assumes the API already runs every earlier main commit, and nothing checks it
#1006's main run went red although #1006 broke nothing it tested
because.evidence: [Job 139335526783](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/echopoint/actions/runs/45651109811/job/139335526783): motion reduced-motion [mobile] failed twice; storybook `Worst Case Table` timed out after a retry; both pass on the next pushes

because.text: Both tests fail on unrelated changes: motion in 3 runs since 2026-11-24, Worst Case Table in 5 runs since 2026-11-22
because.evidence: Scan of the 90 runs with a failed dagger-check among 418 completed Go Build and Test runs, 2026-11-11..25. Main runs: Worst Case Table 8f2e4c6e and bdef245f; motion bdef245f

because.text: Repeat flakes in the frontend checks have no tracker, owner or quarantine, so they keep failing main runs
Why each test flakes (timing of the reduced-motion state on mobile, a 33 s story timeout) is not diagnosed yet
The skew lasted hours and no alert fired
because.evidence: First signal is the routine's own `/health` check, about 2 h after the trigger

because.text: No monitor compares the deployed API commit with main, and a red main run alerts nobody
because.evidence: 2026-11-23 SEV4 ([Atelier](http://nanostack-dev-1340p:4320/postmortems/01a20aeb-3a9c-7ee2-be59-4f6bdf466d7f)) action A3 red-main alert: open, due 2026-12-07

because.text: The postmortem and CI fix went to a spawned task chip that nobody started
because.evidence: No postmortem or PR for row 87 in ci-workflows or echopoint between 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-25

because.text: A ledger row could rest at `mitigated` with its root cause unfixed and its only fix in an unstarted task

contributing: Four frontend-only pushes came within 2.5 hours of the red run, so each green run moved the push-to-push base past #1006.

Each frontend-only run was green, so the newest green commit before the fix (f09065ac) also predates it: the fix covers red runs from now on, and #1006 shipped only because #1013 itself changed a backend pattern.
The `dagger_check` story scope also diffed from `github.event.before`, so a story that failed on a red push was not rerun on the next push.

well: The routine changed the gate flow to accept both behaviours before the stranded backend deployed, so the deploy could not turn the echopoint gate red.
`ci-ok` blocked the backend deploy of a red run, as designed: nothing unverified reached prod's API.
wrong: The same mechanism hit on 2026-11-13 and its fix was never written.

The first version of echopoint #1013 skipped `last_success` on pull requests. GitHub then skipped `migrations-verify`, `migration-lint` and `preview-flag` transitively, and `ci-ok` would still pass. The PR run showed it before the merge.
lucky: Echopoint has about zero users, so a prod web app that called an older API reached nobody.
#1006's frontend and the old API failed in a visible way (missing pages), not by writing wrong data.

Adding `actions: read` directly to `detect-changes.yml` would have failed anchor and atelier at startup, since a called workflow cannot ask for more than its caller grants. The design review caught it before the merge.

actions.what: `last-success-sha.yml` finds the last green push run; `detect-changes.yml` diffs a push from its commit (`base_sha`), else the previous push
echopoint `go.yml` opts in (`last_success` job with `actions: read`), scopes the frontend stories from the same commit, and `ci-ok` fails if the lookup fails
anchor and atelier `go.yml` opt in the same way (last_success never skipped, `actions: read`, `base_sha`, ci-ok gate)
infra Deploy Router `deploy-frontend` promotes to prod only when the prod API runs the newest backend-changing main commit at or before the frontend's commit; otherwise it holds and says why
Diagnose and fix or quarantine the motion reduced-motion [mobile] test and the `Worst Case Table` story, and track repeat frontend flakes with an owner
Alert when main CI is red, or when the API `/health` commit stays behind main's newest backend change for over an hour (2026-11-23 SEV4 action A3)
Postmortem loop: a `mitigated` row with an unfixed root cause gets its fix in the next routine run, never only in a spawned task
Guide lines: ci-workflows AGENTS.md (change detection gates deploys, diff from the last green commit) and echopoint AGENTS.md (a red-run PR ships with the next green push; check `/health`)

messaging.internal: SEV3 echopoint: #1006's backend did not deploy after a red main run (two frontend flakes), while four frontend-only pushes shipped its web app to prod against the old API. Root cause: detect_changes diffed a push only against the previous push. Fixed in ci-workflows #62 and echopoint #1013, which also deploys #1006. Open: anchor/atelier opt-in, an infra frontend-promotion guard, the two flakes, and a red-main alert.
